Group Risk Management Policy

GRP-POL-001|Version6.0|Internal

## 11.5 Quantitative and qualitative assessment

Where reliable data exists, risks are assessed quantitatively — through value-at-risk, expected credit loss modelling, or operational loss distribution approaches. Where data is sparse, assessment is qualitative and structured, using expert judgement captured in facilitated workshops with documented rationale. Qualitative assessments are not inferior, but must state their assumptions explicitly and record who made the judgement.

## 11.6Modelrisk

Models used to quantify risk, price instruments or determine capital are themselves a source of risk. All are registered in the Model Inventory, tiered by materiality, independently validated before first use and revalidated at a frequency set by tier. Model limitations must be disclosed alongside model output wherever that output informs a risk decision. Detailed requirements are in the Model Risk Management Policy (GRP-POL-018), owned by Fatima Z. Qureshi (f.qureshi@cadencefg.com, +91 98213 55228).

## 11.7Aggregation

Risks are aggregated to divisional and Group level using the taxonomy. Aggregation does not average ratings: the profile reports the count and distribution of risks by band, the largest individual exposures, and any concentrations where several separately rated risks share a common cause, control, system or third party.
